page.text:
Cantor's diagonal argument is one of the grand turning points in
intellectual history. It demonstrates that infinity is not a single
monolith: there exists an unending, strictly increasing hierarchy of
infinite cardinalities:
$$|A| < |\mathcal{P}(A)| < |\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(A))| < \dots$$
Moreover, the diagonal technique introduced here is the conceptual
ancestor of the most profound limitative results of modern thought:
Bertrand Russell's refutation of naive comprehension, Kurt Gödel's First
Incompleteness Theorem, and Alan Turing's proof of the undecidability of
the Halting Problem all derive their power from this same
self-referential diagonal architecture.
